summary: This chunk adds two new files documenting an eval run of a 'without_skill' adversarial red-team baseline for a caching design doc. grading.json records 9 expectations checked against the baseline report (6 passed, 3 failed), execution metrics, timing notes, factual claims verified from the design doc, user notes, and eval feedback suggesting a tightened expectation wording. outputs/metrics.json duplicates the same execution metrics (tool calls, files created, output/transcript sizes) as a standalone file.

claims.text: 9 expectations were graded with 6 passed, 3 failed (pass_rate 0.67)
The baseline report flags KEYS-based invalidation as Critical (F-01), ranked above the conditional sizing-collision finding F-07 (High)
Sizing math 40KB x 200k sessions = 8GB matches stated free capacity, flagged as F-07
The report never states an explicit charter or ranked harm-category list before findings
The report gives no single bottom-line verdict statement, and its consolidated fix path covers only 9 of 13 findings
Executor tool calls were Read: 1, Bash: 2, Write: 2 (5 total)
The executor run was killed by a session limit and resumed, with duration covering only the resumed segment
Numeric values in the report's fix directions (timeouts, headroom fractions) are conventional starting points, not measured

risks.note: The same tool-call/step/output metrics are recorded twice in two separate new files with no indication of a single source of truth.

The duration figure and the claim that it 'covers only the resumed segment' are asserted with a pointer to timing.json, but timing.json itself is not part of this chunk, so the number can't be checked here.

least_confident: Whether the 'session limit kill and resume' note in the timing block reflects an actual interruption or is boilerplate, since the referenced timing.json is not included in this chunk.
